issues.legal_issue: An agreement to sell that provides for transfer of possession is deemed a conveyance and is chargeable with the corresponding stamp duty and registration requirements.
Separate agreements executed between different parties as distinct transactions do not qualify for the single-transaction stamp-duty treatment under Section 4 of the Maharashtra Stamp Act.
A later sale deed and stamp duty paid on it do not eliminate the liability to pay the required stamp duty on an earlier agreement to sell that is the principal instrument.
Stamp-duty recovery on the sale deed must be limited to the difference after crediting duty paid on the agreement to sell, while the full applicable penalty remains recoverable.
An impounded agreement cannot be admitted in evidence until the stamp-duty defect is cured under Section 34 of the Maharashtra Stamp Act.
